milestone: UC0 semantic-closure hardening pass — RES-2026-09-14-VELA-EXECUTION-FAILURE-NON-EQUIVALENCE-001 closed the status!==0/errorCode!==0 gap; this pass closes the remaining status===0 gap where evidence itself is missing or malformed.
problem: getVelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome (services/vela/velaMultiPartyProjection.ts) treated EVERY successful completion (status === 0, errorCode === 0) as RESOLVED and passed decryptedUserEventJson straight to parseConfidentialVerdict, which collapses both a legitimate 'not addressed to me' (decryptedUserEventJson === null because no event decrypted for this caller, while other parties' events exist) AND a genuinely broken/missing-evidence case to the SAME 'UNRESOLVED' disposition. Two sub-cases were indistinguishable from a real disposition: (a) a successful completion with ZERO UserEvent logs for the request AT ALL — a fail-closed evidence/protocol defect, since app.go's ProcessRequest path always emits at least one UserEvent on every non-malfunction path, so zero is never legitimate; and (b) an event that DID decrypt for this caller but whose JSON content does not parse as a well-formed {"verdict": ...} payload — malformed evidence, not a genuine decision.
observedFailure: No test exercised userEventCount === 0 or a decrypted-but-malformed event payload before this pass — every prior test either supplied a well-formed verdictFor return or null (modeling ordinary exclusion with other events still existing), so the RESOLVED/UNRESOLVED collapse for these two genuinely-broken cases was never exercised or distinguished.
rootCauses: VelaRequestResult (services/vela/velaTypes.ts) carried no signal for 'how many UserEvent logs exist for this request, to any recipient' — only decryptedUserEventJson (this caller's own decrypted payload, or null). Without that count, the decode layer had no way to distinguish 'zero events exist at all' from 'events exist but none decrypt for me'.

parseConfidentialVerdict's own contract (services/vela/velaProjectionProvider.ts) is, by design, a lossy fail-closed collapse for its own legitimate callers (any non-well-formed input, including null, becomes UNRESOLVED) — appropriate for a single-party caller that wants a conservative disposition, but insufficient on its own for a decode layer that must also distinguish a genuine disposition from missing/broken evidence before persisting anything.
resolution: Added userEventCount: number to VelaRequestResult (services/vela/velaTypes.ts) — total UserEvent logs found for the request, to ANY recipient, computed in VelaClientAdapter.fetchResult (services/vela/velaClientAdapter.ts) from the existing UserEvent queryFilter result (userEvents.length) before the per-recipient decrypt loop runs.

Added the matching userEventCount option (default 1, an event exists somewhere) to VelaTestTransportOptions (services/vela/velaTestTransport.ts), so existing tests that model ordinary not-a-recipient exclusion (verdictFor returning null with other events implicitly existing) are unaffected by default, and a new test can set it to 0 to model the genuinely-missing-event case explicitly.

Added VelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome's 4th branch, {status: 'PROTOCOL_ERROR', reason, applicationFees} (services/vela/velaMultiPartyProjection.ts), and rewrote getVelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome to check, AFTER the existing status/errorCode gate and BEFORE calling parseConfidentialVerdict: (1) result.userEventCount === 0 -> PROTOCOL_ERROR (missing expected event); (2) decryptedUserEventJson !== null && !isWellFormedVerdictJson(decryptedUserEventJson) -> PROTOCOL_ERROR (malformed event content); otherwise -> RESOLVED via the existing parseConfidentialVerdict call, unchanged.

Added the new isWellFormedVerdictJson helper (same file) that asks only whether a non-null JSON string parses as the exact {"verdict": ACCEPTABLE|UNACCEPTABLE|UNRESOLVED} shape parseConfidentialVerdict itself recognises — parseConfidentialVerdict remains the single source of truth for the VALUE; this only distinguishes 'malformed' from 'genuinely resolved' for an event that DID decrypt.

Updated pollMultiPartyDispositionToTerminal (services/vela/velaUnderwritingProjection.ts) to add an explicit PROTOCOL_ERROR throw branch, mirroring its existing EXECUTION_FAILED throw, BEFORE the terminal RESOLVED-only return — so runVelaUnderwritingProjection never quotes, receipts, or telemetry-records a PROTOCOL_ERROR outcome as if it were a genuine disposition.

3rd pass (2026-09-16, same-day correction): the FIRST version of this fix collapsed getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition's PROTOCOL_ERROR into the string 'UNRESOLVED' (item 19, original text, now REVERTED) — on operator review this was identified as re-introducing exactly the conflation this resolution exists to prevent, one call deeper: a coarse caller of the legacy entry point could still receive 'UNRESOLVED' for missing/malformed evidence, indistinguishable from a genuine guest-evidenced refusal. getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition now THROWS distinctly for PROTOCOL_ERROR (naming the reason) instead, while its EXECUTION_FAILED->'UNRESOLVED' collapse is UNCHANGED (an execution failure at least proves the guest never ran, which remains a defensible fail-closed collapse; PROTOCOL_ERROR does not have that property).

3rd pass: proved, using ALREADY-AVAILABLE wire metadata (never inferring 'not addressed' from decrypt failure alone), a genuine partial repair to the 'authorized event that fails to decrypt' distinction the 2nd pass had disclosed as unrepairable: added VelaMalformedCiphertextEnvelopeError (services/vela/velaClientAdapter.ts), thrown by velaDecrypt ONLY for a ciphertext envelope structurally too short (< 28 bytes: 12-byte nonce + 16-byte GCM tag) to be valid for ANY recipient key — proof of wire/storage corruption, never evidence of exclusion, since a correctly encrypted envelope is always that length regardless of which key it was sealed to. The decrypt loop in VelaClientAdapter.fetchResult now counts this distinctly (malformedUserEventCount, new VelaRequestResult field) from an ordinary AES-GCM authentication failure (wrong key OR tampered ciphertext), which remains PROVEN, not merely assumed, indistinguishable by AEAD's own security design (chosen-ciphertext resistance) and by the Vela wire format's own deliberate design (UserEvent.eventSubType is left zero specifically so the on-chain topic reveals nothing about the intended recipient — app.go's own comment). getVelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome gained a new branch: decryptedUserEventJson === null && malformedUserEventCount > 0 -> PROTOCOL_ERROR, naming the count; the residual, genuinely undecidable auth-failure case remains RESOLVED/UNRESOLVED, unchanged.

Added focused regression tests across three passes: tests/vela-multi-party-projection.test.ts (zero-UserEvent PROTOCOL_ERROR, malformed-event-content PROTOCOL_ERROR, malformed-envelope PROTOCOL_ERROR, ordinary-exclusion-unchanged, disposition-throws-distinctly-on-PROTOCOL_ERROR, disposition-still-collapses-EXECUTION_FAILED-unchanged), tests/vela-underwriting-projection.test.ts (PROTOCOL_ERROR throws distinctly, never quotes/receipts/telemetry-records), tests/vela-malformed-ciphertext-envelope.test.ts (new file: VelaMalformedCiphertextEnvelopeError is instanceof-distinguishable from an ordinary AES-GCM auth failure at the exact minimum-length boundary, and never leaks envelope bytes/plaintext/key material in its error message).
rejectedApproaches: Treating result.decryptedUserEventJson === null as PROTOCOL_ERROR directly, without the new userEventCount signal — rejected: this is exactly the legitimate 'authorized event exists for other parties, none decrypt for me' case (VELA-PRIVACY-BOUNDARY-001), which must remain RESOLVED/UNRESOLVED via parseConfidentialVerdict(null), not be reclassified as a protocol defect.

(2nd pass, SUPERSEDED by the 3rd pass above) Declaring 'authorized event that fails to decrypt for a reason other than not-being-the-recipient' entirely out of scope with no further repair attempted — corrected: the STRUCTURAL-malformation subclass (envelope too short for any recipient) IS provably repairable using already-available metadata (the decrypt error's own structural class) without any protocol/architecture change; only the AEAD-auth-failure subclass remains genuinely undecidable, and that residual limitation is now proven (AEAD's own chosen-ciphertext-resistance property, plus the wire format's deliberate zero eventSubType) rather than merely asserted.

(2nd pass, SUPERSEDED by the 3rd pass above) Collapsing getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition's PROTOCOL_ERROR into the string 'UNRESOLVED' to match its existing EXECUTION_FAILED treatment — corrected: this was identified as re-introducing the exact missing-evidence/genuine-disposition conflation this resolution exists to prevent, one call deeper (the legacy entry point's own callers would receive the same fabricated answer the outcome-level fix was built to prevent). The legacy function now throws distinctly for PROTOCOL_ERROR instead; its EXECUTION_FAILED->'UNRESOLVED' collapse is kept, since that case is defensibly different (the guest never ran at all).

Reclassifying an ordinary AES-GCM authentication failure (wrong key or tampered ciphertext) as PROTOCOL_ERROR alongside the structural-malformation subclass — rejected: AEAD's own security definition makes these two causes produce an IDENTICAL failure by design (this is precisely what makes GCM resistant to chosen-ciphertext attacks); reclassifying them would require either weakening that guarantee (never acceptable) or inventing new wire metadata the Vela guest deliberately does not emit (out of scope — 'do not redesign the Vela architecture').

Broadening ConfidentialProjectionDisposition itself with a 4th 'PROTOCOL_ERROR' value — rejected for the same reason RES-2026-09-14-VELA-EXECUTION-FAILURE-NON-EQUIVALENCE-001 rejected a 4th EXECUTION_FAILED disposition value: the distinction is fully addressable at the poll-to-terminal/outcome layer, which is the one place that actually decides whether to persist anything.
